sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Coast Guard Sector San Juan is the service's Caribbean hub, running search and rescue, migrant and drug interdiction, and port security across the waters around Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

Puerto Rico is a U.S. territory, so it's American soil, but a tour here is treated as a non-foreign overseas assignment for pay and logistics: you use the Overseas Housing Allowance (OHA) rather than BAH, with a tropical island setting and a rich Puerto Rican culture.

sections.title: An Island Territory Tour: Tropical and a Bit Different

data.subtitle: Puerto Rico is a U.S. territory that functions like an overseas tour. Most families rent on the local economy with OHA, leaning on the base and the DoDEA school community.
intro: Because Puerto Rico is non-foreign OCONUS, you'll use the Overseas Housing Allowance (OHA) for rentals rather than BAH. Most families live on the local economy around San Juan.

Spanish is the primary language, and island logistics (shipping, power reliability, higher prices for imported goods) are part of the experience, balanced against beaches, culture, and a warm climate year-round.

recommendations.advice: Most families rent around San Juan and the metro using OHA; the housing office helps with the local market and leases.
The base and the DoDEA Antilles school community (Ft Buchanan) anchor family life.
Shipping a vehicle, higher prices for imports, and weather (hurricane season) are part of a PR tour; budget and plan ahead.
Beaches, El Yunque rainforest, and Puerto Rican food and culture make this a memorable tour.

sections.title: Access
data: If family or guests don't have a military ID, ask the sector how visitors get on base before they come.

sections.title: Housing
data: Ask your sponsor and the Coast Guard housing office what housing is open to your family, and whether there is a wait, before you sign a lease.

sections.title: Coast Guard housing at Rio Bayamon
data: The Coast Guard's housing map (updated 10/30/2026) lists the Rio Bayamon housing site, in the Bayamon area west of San Juan, with 141 active homes, the Coast Guard's largest housing site in Puerto Rico.
In the Coast Guard, assignment to Coast Guard housing is generally mandatory when a home is available, and BAH starts only after the housing office releases you to rent in town.

sections.title: Pets
data: Puerto Rico's animal entry rules, as the Military OneSource directory gives them on its Fort Buchanan page: every dog and cat entering Puerto Rico needs an official Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (valid 30 days) stating it did not come from an area under rabies quarantine, a rabies vaccination within six months before shipment for dogs and cats older than 4 months, official identification such as a microchip or a collar with a metal tag, and treatment for external parasites within 72 hours before entry, recorded on the certificate. Dogs and cats coming from a US state do not need a Puerto Rico Department of Agriculture import permit; pets from outside the United States do. Pets arriving by air are picked up at the airline's cargo facility.

According to the Puerto Rico Department of Natural Resources, exotic pets such as snakes, birds and reptiles need pre-approval before they come to the island. Check current rules with USDA APHIS and the Puerto Rico Department of Agriculture before you travel.

source.label: Military OneSource installation directory, Fort Buchanan shipping pets (Puerto Rico entry rules)
